hook: Run an Instagram or Facebook business page? From *Oct 30*, Meta can crawl your website
tldr: Meta's updated terms for business accounts let it use bots and crawlers to access, index, cache and analyse their web pages. Accepting happens just by continuing to use its self-serve ad tools, and accounts can't opt out before Oct 30.

beats.what: The terms apply to any 'business or commercial purpose', including running a Page. Using Ads Manager or Business Suite counts as acceptance.
beats.why: Meta removed the word 'train' but still says it will use the consent to 'develop, improve, research' its products, a wording publishers fear covers AI.
beats.care: Creators and small brands with a website: check Meta's new terms and your site's robots.txt settings.

cards.body: About 3.6 billion people use a Meta app daily and over 200 million businesses use its apps monthly. Its ad revenue hit $59.36 billion in the June quarter, most of it from self-serve advertisers who accept terms with a click.

cards.title: what's robots.txt?
cards.body: A text file on a website that tells crawlers what they may access. Publishers say Meta's new terms don't commit to respecting the latest preferences set there.

cards.q: Should using an ad tool count as agreeing to new data terms?
How do businesses 'accept' Meta's new terms?
opts: By continuing to use its self-serve tools
cards.why: Continued use of Ads Manager or Business Suite counts as acceptance.

viz.l: businesses use Meta apps every month

learn.t: A web crawler is a bot that visits pages automatically to copy and index them. Search engines and AI companies both use them.

watch: Whether Meta clarifies AI training use, and how Indian publishers respond.
